You've seen a dozen of these, so what makes it different from all the other dictation apps? - Local cleanup: We're the only free and open source solution on Windows with a finetuned cleanup model. items.title: Show HN: Perl:CodeMap – Interactive visualization of Perl codebases
items.summary: I came across the recent CodeMap for Go project ( https://github.com/peterretief/codemap ) and decided to adapt it for Perl. It uses PPI for static analysis and generates a self-contained HTML visualization with dependency graphs, searchable modules and subroutines, and syntax-highlighted source browsing. Because of the nature of Perl, it's far from perfect...but functional and a pretty cool tool for a quick map of a codebase. Source: https://github.com/interrupt21h/perl-codemap CPAN: https://metacpan.org/pod/Perl::CodeMap

Show HN: NoDOM high performance WASM UI kit for DuckDB-WASM
items.summary: NoDOM replaces Chrome's DOM, CSS & HTML rendering with a custom WASM engine designed for high performance and minimal latency in Modern Data Oriented C++ for a zero alloc zero copy render hotpath. The aim being to minimise tick-to-render latency. GUI layout and data declarative JSON are served via websocket after initial page load, or can be packaged in an HTML shell like the UK property demo. The layout JSON supports embedded Forth fragments for "glue" computation. NoDOM can also call out to JS both synch and async. NoDOM builds on top of Dear ImGui and ImPlot, and builds to wasm with emscrip
